problemText: In the population regression model mu_y = alpha + beta·x, what does beta represent?
choices: The predicted response y-hat for one particular individual
The population slope: the mean change in y for each one-unit increase in x
The sample slope b computed from one particular data set
The correlation coefficient r between x and y
hints: beta is a population parameter, not a sample statistic.
Compare units: beta describes the mean change in y per unit x in mu_y = alpha + beta·x.

problemText: A residual plot for a regression of exam score on hours of sleep shows about the same amount of vertical scatter above and below zero for small x-values as for large x-values, with no fan or megaphone shape. Which LINER condition does this check?
choices: Equal standard deviation of residuals across all values of x
Independent condition (10% condition)
Nearly Normal distribution of residuals
Random sample or random assignment
hints: Look at whether the vertical scatter changes as x changes.
This condition is about constant variance of the residuals, not their shape or independence.

problemText: Before constructing a t-interval for the slope, a histogram of the residuals is roughly symmetric and bell-shaped with no strong skew or outliers. Which LINER condition does this satisfy?
choices: Linear condition: the residual plot shows no leftover curved pattern
Independent condition: the 10% condition for sampling without replacement
Equal SD condition: consistent vertical spread of residuals
Normal condition: the residuals are nearly normally distributed
hints: Check the shape of the residuals themselves, not the residual-versus-x scatter.
A histogram or Normal probability plot of residuals is the usual check for this condition.

problemText: A random sample of n = 22 (x, y) pairs is used to construct a t-interval for the slope beta of the least-squares regression line. What are the degrees of freedom, df = n − 2? Give a whole number.
hints: df = n − 2 for inference about a single slope, since two parameters (intercept and slope) are estimated from the data.

problemText: A least-squares regression of exam score (y) on hours of sleep (x) for a random sample of n = 22 students gives sample slope b = 3.85 and SE_b = 1.02. For a 95% confidence interval with df = 20, t* = 2.086. Compute the margin of error, t*·SE_b. Round to two decimal places.
hints: Margin of error = t* · SE_b.
Multiply 2.086 by 1.02.

problemText: Using the same regression of exam score on hours of sleep (b = 3.85, margin of error = 2.13), find the upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for beta. Give a number rounded to two decimal places.
hints: Upper bound = b + margin of error.

problemText: A 95% confidence interval for the slope beta, from a regression of exam score on hours of sleep, is (1.72, 5.98). Which is the correct interpretation?
choices: 95% of all students in the population have a slope in this range
There is a 95% probability that the sample slope b itself lies in this interval
We are 95% confident that the interval (1.72, 5.98) captures the true population slope beta relating sleep to exam score
95% of the exam scores in the sample fall between 1.72 and 5.98
hints: A confidence interval statement is about the population parameter beta, not about individual students or the sample slope.
Avoid saying 'probability' about a single already-computed interval.

problemText: An engineer studies x = machine age (years) and y = monthly repair cost (dollars) for a random sample of 18 machines the company owns. To test whether there is a linear relationship between age and repair cost, what is the appropriate null hypothesis?
choices: H0: beta = 0 (no linear relationship between age and repair cost in the population)
H0: b = 0, where b is the slope of this particular sample's regression line
H0: r = 1, indicating a perfect linear relationship
H0: mu_y = 0, the population mean repair cost is zero
hints: The null hypothesis is always stated in terms of the population parameter beta, not the sample statistic b.
'No linear relationship' means the population slope is 0.

problemText: For the sample of n = 18 machines, computer regression output for predicting monthly repair cost (y) from machine age (x) gives slope coefficient b = 18.6 and SE_b = 6.20. Compute the test statistic t = b / SE_b for testing H0: beta = 0. Round to two decimal places.
For the same sample of n = 18 machines used to test H0: beta = 0 for the slope of repair cost on age, what are the degrees of freedom, df = n − 2? Give a whole number.

The regression of monthly repair cost on machine age (n = 18, df = 16) gives t = 3.00 and a two-sided P-value of 0.0086 for testing H0: beta = 0 vs Ha: beta ≠ 0. At alpha = 0.05, what should the engineer conclude?
choices: Fail to reject H0; there is insufficient evidence of a linear relationship between age and repair cost
Reject H0; age causes higher repair costs in every machine
The value 0.0086 IS the population correlation between age and repair cost
Reject H0; since 0.0086 < 0.05 there is convincing evidence of a linear relationship between age and repair cost in the population
hints: Compare the P-value to alpha: 0.0086 < 0.05 means reject H0.
Rejecting H0 supports an association; this is an observational study, not an experiment.

problemText: A separate regression of y = battery life (hours) on x = screen brightness setting, based on a random sample of n = 25 devices, gives sample slope b = -2.4 and SE_b = 0.85. Compute the test statistic t = b / SE_b for testing H0: beta = 0 vs Ha: beta ≠ 0. Round to two decimal places.
hints: t = b / SE_b = -2.4 / 0.85; keep the sign.

problemText: Suppose the repair-cost study instead used a one-sided alternative, Ha: beta > 0 (repair cost increases with age), and the sample slope b = 18.6 is positive, matching the direction of Ha. The computer output reports a two-sided P-value of 0.0086 for testing H0: beta = 0. What is the correct P-value for this one-sided test?
choices: 0.0086, unchanged, because P-values never depend on the direction of Ha
0.0043, half the two-sided P-value, since the sample slope points in the direction of Ha
0.0172, double the two-sided P-value
It cannot be determined without re-running the regression
hints: Computer output reports a two-sided P-value by default.
Halve it only when the sample slope's sign matches the direction of Ha.

problemText: A test of H0: beta = 0 yields strong evidence to reject H0 in favor of Ha: beta ≠ 0 for the regression of repair cost on machine age. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: Older machine age directly causes higher repair costs, since the test rejected H0
The population slope beta must equal exactly 18.6, the sample estimate
There is convincing evidence of a linear association between age and repair cost in the population represented by the sample, but causation cannot be concluded from this observational study
The large sample size guarantees a causal relationship
hints: A small P-value shows evidence of linear association, not cause and effect.
Only a randomized experiment can support a causal claim.
